comments.author: @sandeeplotlikar9365
comments.text:
I must address the clear bias in this video about Mumbai. It deliberately focuses only on the city’s challenges and a handful of specific areas, while completely ignoring the vibrant, beautiful, and modern side of Mumbai that millions admire and experience every day.
Mumbai is one of the most iconic and dynamic cities in the world. The video conveniently skips iconic landmarks and attractions such as Marine Drive, Nariman Point, the Gateway of India, Colaba, Juhu Beach, the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Siddhivinayak Temple, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nehru Planetarium, and many more. It also fails to show the city’s world-class infrastructure — including the impressive Mumbai Metro, its bustling international airport, sprawling malls, and the bustling business districts in Parel and beyond that house numerous multinational companies.
This selective portrayal creates a misleading and distorted image. By highlighting only certain poorer neighborhoods, the video falsely implies that Mumbai is dominated by a particular community, which is entirely inaccurate and far from reality. Mumbai is a true melting pot — cosmopolitan, diverse, and home to people from every religion, region, and background who coexist and contribute to its energy. The depiction of gender dynamics and social issues is equally one-sided and does not reflect the progressive, modern outlook that defines much of the city and its residents.
Such videos are not authentic journalism or honest documentation — they are agenda-driven narratives designed to tarnish the image of Mumbai and, by extension, India. The creators cherry-pick visuals and half-truths to paint a grim, exaggerated picture while deliberately omitting everything positive and aspirational. As the saying goes, a half-truth is often as damaging as a complete lie. These tactics mislead viewers, especially those unfamiliar with India, and reveal the questionable intentions behind such content.
Genuine creators highlight both strengths and weaknesses in a balanced manner. When someone consistently avoids the beauty, achievements, and spirit of a place while amplifying only negativity, it exposes their bias and lack of integrity. Mumbai — and India — deserves fair representation, not propaganda disguised as video content.

replies.author: @ChosenOne563
replies.text:
Look, the reality is that Mumbai has huge slums, poor sanitation, narrow and unplanned roads, and electricity cables hanging everywhere. If you look at many utility poles, they're covered with a mess of wires, and you'll often see kites, plastic bags, and other rubbish stuck in them. It doesn't exactly give the impression of a well-planned city.
There are still neighborhoods with open sewage drains, and many areas have grown without proper urban planning. The city is so overcrowded that in some places it's difficult to even walk comfortably because the streets are packed, footpaths are occupied, or they're simply not maintained properly.
You can't judge the whole city by pointing to a few modern areas. Just because there are some clean, well-developed neighborhoods where wealthy people, actors, and industrialists live doesn't mean the entire city is like that. Those are exceptions, not the reality for most people.
And honestly, this isn't just a Mumbai problem. You'll find similar issues in many cities across South Asia, especially in India. A lot of cities have expanded based on immediate needs rather than long-term planning. Infrastructure has struggled to keep up with the rapid population growth.
Garbage management is another major issue. In many places, bins overflow, and on some streets there aren't enough public bins at all. People throw rubbish on the roadside, others keep adding to the same spot, and before long it turns into a huge pile of garbage.
Public hygiene is also a challenge. It's still common to see people spitting after chewing paan, and in some places people urinate in public. Despite improvements over the years, these issues still exist.
So I can't agree with the claim that Mumbai is a clean city just because a few areas look modern. Every big city has its wealthy neighborhoods, but that doesn't represent the city as a whole. Mumbai has many great things—it's India's financial capital and has world-class businesses—but when it comes to cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, and urban planning, it still has a long way to go compared with many well-planned cities in Europe, North America, or East Asia.

comments.author: @jeetendrapatil6799
comments.text:
I'm from a city near Mumbai watching your videos regularly.
I saw your video, and while it does highlight certain realities of Mumbai, it only shows one side of the city. Mumbai is much more than crowded or underdeveloped areas—it’s a place of immense opportunity, resilience, and diversity.

This city is India’s financial capital and home to world-class infrastructure, iconic landmarks, a thriving business ecosystem, and one of the most dynamic cultures in the country. People from all backgrounds come here with dreams, and many build successful lives through hard work and determination.

What truly defines Mumbai is its spirit—the way people support each other, stay strong during challenges, and keep moving forward. Alongside its struggles, there is innovation, growth, cleanliness in many areas, beautiful sea fronts, and a vibrant lifestyle that deserves equal attention.

A balanced view would show both realities. Mumbai is not perfect, but it is inspiring in ways that go far beyond what your video captures.
